//: Gate caps for `make bench-gate` (bench/run.mjs --gate): the MAX acceptable new/base ratio of median-of-launches ns/op, Lava against a baseline Lava (default origin/master). Every benchmark is gated by its entry in caps, else default_cap, unless listed in report_only. The Node-ratio caps this file held until the Node profile went (#130) measured a different quantity and were dropped, not converted.
//calibration: Measured 2026-11-27 on a 4-core Linux x86_64 box, bin/lava -o:speed: 4 A/A runs of `BASE=bin/lava node bench/run.mjs` (same binary both sides, BENCH_LAUNCHES=5, medians of 5 interleaved launches per side). Over 34 benchmarks x 4 runs, the A/A ratio stayed within 0.77x-1.30x for 32 benchmarks (worst: headers-get 1.30x, urlsearchparams-get 0.77x/1.25x, url-relative 1.20x/0.79x, response-new 1.27x). default_cap 1.5 sits ~1.15x above that worst case: medium confidence from 4 runs, and it detects a slowdown of roughly 1.5x, not 10%. Two benchmarks are report-only because their A/A spread is the size of the regression a cap would exist to catch: blob-slice measured 0.55x, 1.04x, 1.29x, 0.88x (bimodal: 145 ns vs 261 ns per op in the same binary) and decode-utf16le 1.06x, 1.11x, 0.80x, 1.68x. Re-measure A/A before tightening anything.
